nodes.title: SG-5.6.2 Scene unit tests with Phaser mocked cover the scene behaviors through the @game alias
nodes.body:
Context: game/tests has scene tests (layers, buildScene, sceneObject, interaction, preload) that import source with relative paths. game/vitest.config.ts defines the @game and phaser aliases, but game/tsconfig.json has no @game path mapping. Desired behavior: a scene suite imports real, existing source through @game, mocks Phaser, covers the five behaviors and passes together. Expected result: one command runs the suite green, and tsc resolves @game. Why: the sub-goal SG-5.6.2 needs proof that the scene behaviors are tested against real files.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the game tsconfig, when tsc resolves '@game/engine/layers', then it maps to game/src/engine/layers.ts
- Given the scene suite files, when they run together under vitest, then every test passes with Phaser mocked
- Given the suite, when its imports are read, then every source import uses the @game alias and names an existing file
- Given the suite, when it runs, then it asserts layer ordering, content-to-entity creation, visibility conditions, hover and click, and the missing-asset fallback


## Scope
- In scope: game/tsconfig.json @game paths
- In scope: scene unit tests under game/tests
- Out of scope: backend
- Out of scope: new gameplay behavior
- Out of scope: browser or e2e checks
- Preserve: game/vitest.config.ts aliases
- Preserve: existing tests
- Preserve: public APIs of src/engine and src/entities


## Technical constraints
- Phaser must be mocked in tests
- Tests import real source via @game, not mocks of it


## Definition of done
- All three requirements have Act and Verify units done
- Scene suite passes together


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · game tsconfig resolves the @game alias
nodes.body:
Context: vitest.config.ts maps @game to ./src but game/tsconfig.json has no paths, so tests importing @game fail typecheck. Desired behavior: tsconfig maps @game/* to src/*. Expected result: npm run typecheck resolves @game imports. Why: tests must import through the alias.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given game/tsconfig.json, when parsed, then compilerOptions.paths['@game/*'] equals ['./src/*']
- Given a test importing '@game/engine/layers', when tsc runs, then no module-not-found error is reported


## Scope
- In scope: game/tsconfig.json
- Out of scope: frontend tsconfig
- Preserve: strict, include and other compiler options


## Technical constraints
- moduleResolution Bundler stays


## Definition of done
- paths entry present
- typecheck resolves @game


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Scene suite proves layer ordering, content-to-entity creation and visibility via @game
nodes.body:
Context: layers.ts, buildScene.ts and SceneObject.ts exist; buildScene sorts SceneObject by depth and sync() applies visibleWhen via evaluateAll. Desired behavior: one suite asserts these through @game with a fake RenderContext. Expected result: suite passes. Why: confirms SG-5.6.2 areas 1-3.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given objects authored in furniture, background, objects order, when buildScene runs, then depths come back ascending background, furniture, objects
- Given a scene with N objects, when buildScene runs, then createSprite is called N times with each spec's asset, position and scale
- Given an object with visibleWhen flag, when sync runs with the flag false then true, then setVisible receives false then true


## Scope
- In scope: layer ordering
- In scope: content-to-entity creation
- In scope: visibility conditions
- Out of scope: Phaser rendering
- Preserve: existing buildScene, sceneObject and layers tests


## Technical constraints
- Fake RenderContext, no real Phaser


## Dependencies
- REQ-A


## Definition of done
- suite green


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Scene suite proves hover, click and missing-asset fallback with Phaser mocked via @game
nodes.body:
Context: SceneObject wires onHover/onClick; BootScene (frontend/src/phaser/BootScene.ts) uses planPreload and resolveTextureKey with FALLBACK_KEY. Desired behavior: suite asserts these through @game with phaser mocked. Expected result: passes together with REQ-B suite. Why: confirms SG-5.6.2 areas 4-5.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a visible object, when hover is true then false, then setHighlighted and setLabelVisible get true then false
- Given a visible synced object, when click fires, then the listener receives objectId and available actions; a hidden object emits nothing
- Given an asset id absent from the manifest, when resolveTextureKey runs, then it returns the fallback key
- Given a scene referencing an unknown asset, when preload runs, then it is not loaded and the fallback texture is generated


## Scope
- In scope: hover
- In scope: click
- In scope: fallback texture
- Out of scope: real Phaser rendering
- Preserve: tests/preload.test.ts


## Technical constraints
- Mock 'phaser' and frontend runtime modules with vi.mock


## Dependencies
- REQ-A


## Definition of done
- suite green


## Clarifying questions
- None
